title: Fields, curves and Frobenius
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, and put $q=p^a$. Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ be the fixed field with $q$ elements [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements], and choose an algebraic closure $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of $k_0$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, write $\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and fix a field embedding $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$ (an injective unital field homomorphism, with no continuity condition).

In this chapter a *curve* $C_0/\mathbf F_q$ is a nonempty scheme [def-pc-scheme] over $k_0$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose structure morphism is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], such that $C_0$ has pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension] and its base change $C=C_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-base-change] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

For a closed point $x$ of $C_0$ [def-weil-closed-points], write $\kappa(x)$ for its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], and put $e_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]$ [def-weil-closed-point-degree] and $q_x=q^{e_x}$.

Throughout this chapter, *Frobenius* means geometric Frobenius $F=\varphi_q^{-1}$ on $k$, where $\varphi_q(t)=t^q$ [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. Its local version $F_x$ is geometric Frobenius of the finite residue field $\kappa(x)$: on a chosen algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ it is the inverse of $t\mapsto t^{q_x}$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-frobenius-substitution].

An *affine open* of $C_0$ in this chapter means a nonempty open subscheme $U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ [def-weil-open-immersion] isomorphic over $k_0$ to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] for a finitely generated $k_0$-algebra $A$ (one generated as a $k_0$-algebra by finitely many elements, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]).
